status_summary: Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) renamed global intangible low-taxed income as net CFC tested income and set the section 250 deduction for it at 40 percent from tax years beginning after 2025, replacing the 50 percent deduction and striking the scheduled cut to 37.5 percent. With the 21 percent corporate rate this gives about 12.6 percent before credits, slightly above the 12.5 percent ceiling, below the roughly 13.1 percent rate scheduled under prior law, and above the 10.5 percent rate in effect through 2025. The same law raised the deemed-paid foreign tax credit share from 80 to 90 percent, halving the haircut, while adding a separate 10 percent credit disallowance for taxes on distributions of previously taxed income. The estate and gift tax top rate remains 40 percent in the Code.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 section 70321 set the section 250 deduction at 40 percent of net CFC tested income (formerly GILTI) and struck the scheduled reduction to 37.5 percent, effective for taxable years beginning after 2025.

Public Law 119-21 section 70312 raised the deemed paid foreign tax credit percentage in 26 U.S.C. 960(d) from 80 to 90 percent for taxable years beginning after 2025 and added a disallowance of 10 percent of foreign taxes on distributions of previously taxed income, applying to such taxes paid, accrued or deemed paid after 2025-06-28.

title: Cut GILTI tax to 12.5 percent or less and the estate and gift tax rate to 20 percent
uncertainties: Route read: Cornell Legal Information Institute copies of 26 U.S.C. 250, 960 and 2001 with their Public Law 119-21 notes (reread in this review), plus the official enrolled text on govinfo.gov, of which only the opening part (the table of contents and title I) could be loaded; that part confirms the section numbers and headings of sections 70312, 70321, 70322 and 70323 but not their operative text, so the substance rests on the Cornell copy, which is not the official Code. The researcher read section 2010 and the H.R. 1 bill status record. The 12.6 percent and 13.1 percent figures are arithmetic (21 percent times 60 percent and times 62.5 percent) and ignore the section 78 gross-up, expense allocation and other base changes, so effective rates vary by taxpayer. The Cornell page for section 2001 shows a 40 percent top bracket and no 2025 amendment. The 10 percent credit disallowance applies to covered foreign taxes arising after 2025-06-28, earlier than the tax-year rules for the other changes. Section 70106 raised the estate and gift basic exclusion amount to 15,000,000 dollars from 2026 (per the Cornell copy of section 2010), which concerns the exemption rather than the rate tracked here. Which baseline to use for the rate is a judgment: the text, written in 2023, faced a scheduled increase to about 13.1 percent, so 12.6 percent is a reduction from that schedule but an increase from the 10.5 percent rate in force through 2025. The GILTI items also appear in c22-02, which does not cover the estate tax rate.
